info.title: LCARS API
info.summary: LCARS for home: the HTTP side of the LCARS home display API.
info.description:
The LCARS home display API is served primarily over **NATS**, with protobuf message bodies. This reference covers the HTTP server that runs alongside it: a health check, these docs, and JSON versions of the NATS endpoints for debugging and simple clients.

## NATS API

Devices connect to the NATS server lcars-api runs (port `4222` by default) or to the one it is configured to use. Message bodies are protobuf messages defined in [`proto/lcars/v1`](https://github.com/asilluron/lcars-api/tree/main/proto/lcars/v1); generated Rust (prost) types are in the `lcars-proto` crate in [`rust/`](https://github.com/asilluron/lcars-api/tree/main/rust).

| Subject | Kind | Messages | HTTP equivalent |
|---------|------|----------|-----------------|
| `lcars.calendar.get` | request/reply | `GetCalendarRequest` → `GetCalendarResponse` | [`GET /calendar`](#operation/getCalendar) |
| `lcars.calendar.updated` | event | `CalendarUpdated`, published when the `.ics` files change | none |

NATS error replies have an empty body and the headers `Nats-Service-Error-Code` (the same status code the HTTP endpoint would return) and `Nats-Service-Error` (the message). The service is named `lcars`, so it also answers `$SRV.PING.lcars`, `$SRV.INFO.lcars` and `$SRV.STATS.lcars`.

This reference is generated from the OpenAPI document the server itself serves at [`/openapi.json`](/openapi.json), and the version shown above is the version of the running build.

## Conventions

- **Encoding.** Request and response bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`) unless an operation says otherwise.
- **`HEAD`.** Every `GET` operation also answers `HEAD`, with the same status and headers and no body.
- **Authentication.** None, over HTTP or NATS. The API is meant to run on a trusted home network; put it behind a reverse proxy if you need authentication or TLS.
- **Dates and times.** Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Timestamps are [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) with the UTC offset of the server's timezone, e.g. `2026-10-20T09:00:00-04:00`.
- **Versioning.** Paths are not versioned yet. The build version is reported by [`GET /healthz`](#operation/getHealth).

## Errors

Errors raised by an operation have a JSON body with a single `error` field:

```json
{"error": "Internal Server Error"}
```

Unexpected failures, including panics, are logged on the server and returned as a `500` with a generic message, so internal details never reach the client.

Routing errors come from the router before any operation runs, and have a **plain-text** body:

| Status | When | Body |
|--------|------|------|
| `404` | No route matches the path. | `404 page not found` |
| `405` | The path exists, but not for this method. The `Allow` header lists the methods that are, e.g. `Allow: GET, HEAD`. | `Method Not Allowed` |

## Timeouts

The server closes connections that are slow to send headers (5 s) or a request (15 s), and responses that take longer than 15 s to write. Idle keep-alive connections are closed after 60 s. On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` it stops accepting new connections and waits for in-flight requests to finish before exiting.

tags.name: Calendar
tags.description:
Events read from `.ics` files on the host.

The server reads every `.ics` file under the directory set by `calendar.dir` in the config file (or `LCARS_CALENDAR_DIR`), including subdirectories, and re-reads it every `calendar.refresh_interval` (default one hour). Recurring events are expanded, including exceptions (`EXDATE`) and edited or cancelled occurrences (`RECURRENCE-ID`). A file that can't be parsed is skipped and logged on the server; the rest are still served.

Each event belongs to a calendar, named by the file's `X-WR-CALNAME` if set, otherwise by the top-level subdirectory the file is in, otherwise by the file name without `.ics`. So both `calendars/family.ics` and `calendars/family/*.ics` give a calendar named `family`.

get.description: Reports that the process is up, along with the build version and the state of the NATS connection the API is served on. Answers `503` while that connection is down (for example, while an external NATS server is restarting); lcars-api reconnects on its own. It does no other work, so it is cheap to call often.

200.description: The server is up and connected to NATS.

503.description: The server is up, but its NATS connection is down, so NATS clients can't reach it.

get.description:
Returns the events in a range of days, grouped by day, ready to draw as an agenda or week view. Every day in the range is present, in order, even if it has no events.

Dates and times are in the server's timezone (`timezone` in the config file, or the host's), which the response reports. An event that spans several days appears on each of them. Within a day, all-day events come first, then timed events by start time.

Events are read from disk periodically, not on each request; `updated_at` says when they were last read.

The same data is available over NATS as a protobuf `GetCalendarResponse`, by sending a `GetCalendarRequest` on `lcars.calendar.get`. Subscribe to `lcars.calendar.updated` to learn when to fetch it again.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day to list, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to today in the server's timezone.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of days to list, starting with `from`.

example.error: invalid "days": want a whole number from 1 to 62
calendar is not configured: set calendar.dir in the config file

get.description: Returns this OpenAPI 3.1 document, with `info.version` set to the version of the running build. Import it into an API client, or generate a typed client from it.

Returns the HTML page you are reading: a [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc) rendering of [`/openapi.json`](#operation/getOpenAPI). The page loads Redoc from a CDN, pinned to one version and checked with Subresource Integrity, so the browser viewing it needs internet access.

status.description: `ok` if the server is fully working; `unavailable` if its NATS connection is down.

version.description: Build version: the release tag (or `git describe` output) the binary was built from, or `(devel)` for an unversioned local build.

nats.description: State of the NATS connection the API is served on.

error.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

timezone.description: IANA name of the timezone all dates and times are in, or `Local` if the host's zone has no known name.

updated_at.description: When the `.ics` files were last read successfully.

days.description: One entry per day from `from` to `to`, in order.

today.description: Whether this day is today in the server's timezone.

events.description: Events overlapping this day: all-day events first, then by start time. Empty if there are none.

id.description: Identifies this occurrence: the event's `UID`, a slash, and its start time in UTC. Each occurrence of a recurring event has its own ID, and a multi-day event has the same ID on every day.

title.description: The event's `SUMMARY`. Empty if it has none.

calendar.description: Name of the calendar the event is from. See the Calendar section above for how it is chosen.

location.description: The event's `LOCATION`. Empty if it has none.

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day event. All-day events have no times: `start` and `end` are midnights, and `start_time` and `end_time` are null.

end.description: When the occurrence ends (exclusive). For an all-day event on one day, this is midnight at the start of the next day.

start_time.description: Start time as `HH:MM` (24-hour), if a timed event starts on this day; null otherwise. Use it as the display label without parsing `start`.

end_time.description: End time as `HH:MM` (24-hour), if a timed event ends on this day; null otherwise. An event ending exactly at midnight shows `24:00` on the day before.

InternalError.description: The server failed unexpectedly. Details are logged on the server, not returned.
